metadata.title: On the construction of non-$2$-colorable uniform hypergraphs

extraction_notes.note: Tables 1 and 2 list best-known bounds on m(n) for n<=17 (including m(13)<=297347 and m(17)<=13201419, stated only in Table 2); table rows were not made nodes.
The custom 'Result' environment has no standard type; typed theorem, since these are the paper's main stated results, proved later by the hyperedge counts and Lemmas 3-5.

Results 1-3 are restated verbatim in Sections 3-5 after the counting arguments; the restated inequalities got no node (one node per repeated statement) and the counting paragraphs became prose proofs of the Result environments.

Sections 3-5 repeat the Section 2 notation sentences (m_{n-2}, Y, U, V, matching vertices, U_K, V_K, complements), Section 5 with n=8; these restatements got no nodes and the Section 2 definitions carry the edges.
Each hypergraph construction (steps (i)-(vii)) could be a definition of H; typed algorithm per the step-by-step procedure rule, one algorithm_step per listed step.

nodes.name: Property B
nodes.statement: A hypergraph is said to have property B if there exists a proper subset $\textit{S}$ of its vertices such that every hyperedge of the hypergraph contains vertices from both $\textit{S}$ and $\textit{$\overline{S}$}$, the complement of $S$. In other words, if the vertices of a hypergraph can be colored using Red and Blue colors such that every hyperedge of the hypergraph contains Red as well as Blue vertices, then that hypergraph is said to have {\it Property B}.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
differentia: there exists a proper subset $\textit{S}$ of its vertices such that every hyperedge of the hypergraph contains vertices from both $\textit{S}$ and $\textit{$\overline{S}$}$
nodes.statement_short: A hypergraph has Property B (is 2-colorable) if its vertices can be Red/Blue colored with no monochromatic hyperedge.

nodes.name: 2-colorable hypergraphs with many hyperedges
nodes.statement: It is known that there exist $2$-colorable hypergraphs with arbitrarily high number of hyperedges.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
conclusions: there exist $2$-colorable hypergraphs with arbitrarily high number of hyperedges

nodes.name: Lovász Problem 13.33
nodes.statement: For example, Lov\'{a}sz mentions the following in Problem $13.33$ of \cite{Lovasz}: if there are no two hyperedges with exactly one common vertex in a hypergraph, then the hypergraph is $2$-colorable.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: there are no two hyperedges with exactly one common vertex in a hypergraph
nodes.statement_short: A hypergraph in which no two hyperedges share exactly one vertex is 2-colorable.

nodes.name: m(n)
nodes.statement: The least possible number of hyperedges in an $n$-uniform hypergraph which does not have Property B is denoted by $m(n)$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Non-2-colorable hypergraphs and unsatisfiable monotone CNF
nodes.statement: In fact, constructing a non-$2$-colorable $n$-uniform hypergraph $H$ with $x$ hyperedges is equivalent to constructing an unsatisfiable monotone $n$-CNF with $2x$ clauses.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
conclusions: constructing a non-$2$-colorable $n$-uniform hypergraph $H$ with $x$ hyperedges is equivalent to constructing an unsatisfiable monotone $n$-CNF with $2x$ clauses

nodes.name: CNF H' of a hypergraph
nodes.statement: For a given $n$-uniform hypergraph $H$, let $H'$ denote the $n$-CNF obtained by adding clauses $C_{e}:= (x_{1} \vee x_{2} \dots \vee x_{n})$ and $\bar C_{e}:= (\bar x_{1} \vee \bar x_{2} \dots \vee \bar x_{n})$ for every hyperedge $e$ = $\{x_{1},x_{2}, \dots,x_{n}\} \in H$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: $H'$ has, for every hyperedge, the all-positive and the all-negated clause on its vertices.

nodes.name: monotone CNF
nodes.statement: Note that $H'$ is monotone, i.e., every clause of $H'$ either contains only non-negated literals or only negated literals.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
differentia: every clause of $H'$ either contains only non-negated literals or only negated literals

nodes.name: 2-colorings correspond to satisfying assignments
nodes.statement: It can be easily seen that every $2$-coloring $\chi$ of $H$ yields a satisfying assignment $\alpha$ of $H'$ and vice versa.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
conclusions: every $2$-coloring $\chi$ of $H$ yields a satisfying assignment $\alpha$ of $H'$ and vice versa

nodes.name: Erdős and Beck lower bounds on m(n)
nodes.statement: Erd\H{o}s \cite{erdos1} showed that $m(n) = \Omega({2^n})$, which was improved to $\Omega({n^{1/3 - o(1)} 2^n})$ by Beck \cite{beck}.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan lower bound
nodes.statement: It was further improved by Radhakrishnan and Srinivasan \cite{radhakrishnan} to the currently best known lower bound $m(n)=\Omega({\sqrt{\frac{n}{\ln n}} 2^n})$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Erdős probabilistic upper bound
nodes.statement: In the other direction, Erd\H{o}s \cite{erdos} used the probabilistic method to show that $m(n) = O(n^2 2^n)$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Gebauer construction
nodes.statement: Recently, Gebauer \cite{geba} provided a construction which produces a non-$2$-colorable $n$-uniform hypergraph containing $2^n \cdot 2^{O(n^{\frac{2}{3}})}$ hyperedges for a sufficiently large $n$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: m(2)=3 and m(3)=7
nodes.statement: It is straightforward to see that $m(2) = 3$ (triangle graph) and $m(3) = 7$ (Fano plane \cite{klein}).
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Abbott–Hanson bound m(4) ≤ 24
nodes.statement: The construction of Abbott and Hanson \cite{Abbott} proved that $m(4) \leq 24$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Seymour bound m(4) ≤ 23
nodes.statement: Seymour \cite{seymour} improved upon this construction to show that $m(4) \leq 23$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Manning bound m(4) ≥ 21
nodes.statement: In the other direction, Manning \cite{manning} provided a proof that $m(4) \geq 21$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Östergård bound m(4) ≥ 23
nodes.statement: Recently, \"{O}sterg\r{a}rd \cite{patric} has proved that $m(4) \geq 23$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: m(4)=23
nodes.statement: This shows that $m(4) = 23$, and settles this problem for $n = 4$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Exact value of m(n) for n ≥ 5
nodes.statement: The problem of finding the exact value of $m(n)$ for $n\geq 5$ still remains an open problem.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Abbott–Moser product bound
nodes.statement: They proved that if $n$ = $a \cdot b$ such that $a$ and $b$ are integer factors of $n$, then $m(n) \leq m(a) \cdot (m(b))^a$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: $n$ = $a \cdot b$ such that $a$ and $b$ are integer factors of $n$

nodes.name: Abbott–Moser construction
nodes.statement: Take an $a$-uniform hypergraph giving the best known value for $m(a)$ and replace the vertices of this hypergraph with different $b$-uniform hypergraphs that gives the best known value for $m(b)$. Note that the vertex set of each of these $b$-uniform hypergraphs must be disjoint from each other. In order to form an $n$-uniform hyperedge, the hyperedges of these $a$ different $b$-uniform hypergraphs are combined with each other in every possible way.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
input: an $a$-uniform hypergraph giving the best known value for $m(a)$
different $b$-uniform hypergraphs that gives the best known value for $m(b)$
nodes.statement_short: Substitute a copy of an optimal b-uniform hypergraph for each vertex of an optimal a-uniform hypergraph and take all combinations of their hyperedges.

nodes.name: Abbott–Moser hyperedge count
nodes.statement: Therefore, the $n$-uniform hypergraph has a total of $m(a) \cdot (m(b))^a$ hyperedges.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
conclusions: the $n$-uniform hypergraph has a total of $m(a) \cdot (m(b))^a$ hyperedges

nodes.name: Abbott–Hanson recurrence
nodes.statement: The second construction is by Abbott and Hanson \cite{Abbott} which gives the recurrence $m(n) \leq 2^{n-1} + n \cdot m(n-2)$ when $n$ is odd.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Toft recurrence
nodes.statement: The third construction is by Toft \cite{toft2}, who obtained the following bound when $n$ is even: $m(n) \leq 2^{n-1} + {n \choose {n / 2}} / {2} + n \cdot m(n-2)$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Result 1: first improved recurrence for m(n)
nodes.statement: We provide a construction which shows that $m(n) \leq (n+1) \cdot 2^{n-2} + \linebreak (n-1) \cdot m(n-2)$ when $n$ is odd, and $m(n) \leq (n+1) \cdot 2^{n-2} + {n \choose {n / 2}}/{2} + (n-1) \cdot \left( m(n-2) + {n-2 \choose {(n-2)}/{2}} \right)$ when $n$ is even.
nodes.section: 1.1 Our contribution
nodes.statement_short: Recurrence $m(n) \le (n+1)2^{n-2} + (n-1)m(n-2)$ for odd $n$, with an analogous even-$n$ bound.

nodes.name: Result 2: second improved recurrence for m(n)
nodes.statement: We provide a construction which shows that $m(n) \leq (n+4) \cdot 2^{n-3} + \linebreak (n-2) \cdot m(n-2)$ when $n$ is odd, and $m(n) \leq (n+4) \cdot 2^{n-3} + n \cdot {n-2 \choose {(n-2)/2}}/{2} + {n \choose {n / 2}}/{2} + (n-2) \cdot m(n-2)$ when $n$ is even.
nodes.section: 1.1 Our contribution
nodes.statement_short: Recurrence $m(n) \le (n+4)2^{n-3} + (n-2)m(n-2)$ for odd $n$, with an analogous even-$n$ bound.

nodes.statement: We show that $m(11) \leq 25449$, which improves the currently best known bound $m(11) \leq 27435$.

nodes.name: core hypergraph
nodes.statement: For a given $n \geq 3$, let us consider an $(n-2)$-uniform hypergraph producing the best known upper bound for $m(n-2)$. We denote this hypergraph as a {\it core hypergraph}.
nodes.section: 2 The construction of Abbott and Hanson \cite{Abbott}, and Toft \cite{toft2}
differentia: producing the best known upper bound for $m(n-2)$

nodes.name: m_{n-2} and C=(X,Y)
nodes.statement: Let $m_{n-2}$ be the number of hyperedges present in this core hypergraph $C =(X, Y)$.
nodes.section: 2 The construction of Abbott and Hanson \cite{Abbott}, and Toft \cite{toft2}

nodes.name: hyperedge set Y
nodes.statement: The set of hyperedges is denoted by $Y = \{e_1, e_2, e_3, \ldots, e_{m_{n-2}}\}$, where $e_i$ is the $i^{th}$ hyperedge in the core hypergraph $C$.
nodes.section: 2 The construction of Abbott and Hanson \cite{Abbott}, and Toft \cite{toft2}

nodes.name: vertex sets U and V
nodes.statement: Let $U = \{u_1, u_2, u_3, \ldots, u_n\}$ and $V = \{v_1, v_2, v_3, \ldots, v_n\}$ denote two disjoint set of vertices, each of them disjoint from $X$, the set of vertices in the core hypergraph $C$.
nodes.section: 2 The construction of Abbott and Hanson \cite{Abbott}, and Toft \cite{toft2}

nodes.name: matching vertices
nodes.statement: For each $1 \leq i \leq n$, we call $u_i$ and $v_i$ to be a pair of {\it matching vertices}.
nodes.section: 2 The construction of Abbott and Hanson \cite{Abbott}, and Toft \cite{toft2}

nodes.name: U_K and V_K
nodes.statement: For any $K = \{a_1, a_2, \ldots a_k\}$ which is a proper subset of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ such that $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 \ldots < a_k \leq n$, we denote $U_K = \{u_{a_1}, u_{a_2}, \ldots, u_{a_k}\}$ and $V_K = \{v_{a_1}, v_{a_2}, \ldots, v_{a_k}\}$.
nodes.section: 2 The construction of Abbott and Hanson \cite{Abbott}, and Toft \cite{toft2}

nodes.name: complements of U_K and V_K
nodes.statement: We also define ${\bar{U}}_K = U \setminus U_K$ and ${\bar{V}}_K = V \setminus V_K$.
nodes.section: 2 The construction of Abbott and Hanson \cite{Abbott}, and Toft \cite{toft2}

nodes.name: AHT construction
nodes.statement: Let us now define the construction of the non-$2$-colorable $n$-uniform hypergraph $H$. The vertex set of this hypergraph is $X \cup U \cup V$, and the following hyperedges are present in $H$:\\ $(i)$ $\{u_i\} \cup e_j \cup \{v_i\}$ for every pair of $i, j$ satisfying $1 \leq i \leq n$ and $1 \leq j \leq m_{n-2}$. $(ii)$ $U$ $(iii)$ $U_K \cup {\bar{V}}_K$ for every $K$ such that $|K|$ is odd, and $1 \leq |K| \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. $(iv)$ $V_K \cup {\bar{U}}_K$ for every $K$ such that $|K|$ is even, and $2 \leq |K| \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.section: 2 The construction of Abbott and Hanson \cite{Abbott}, and Toft \cite{toft2}
input: an $(n-2)$-uniform hypergraph producing the best known upper bound for $m(n-2)$
nodes.statement_short: Abbott–Hanson–Toft: pad each core hyperedge with each matching pair, add $U$ and the parity-alternating sets $U_K\cup\bar V_K$, $V_K\cup\bar U_K$.

nodes.name: Hyperedge count of the AHT construction
nodes.statement: Note that the total number of hyperedges in this hypergraph is \\ $1 + \binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2} + \ldots + \binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} + n \cdot m_{n-2}$. \\ \noindent When $n$ is odd, this shows that $m(n) \leq 2^{n-1} + n \cdot m(n-2)$. \noindent When $n$ is even, this shows that $m(n) \leq 2^{n-1} + {n \choose {n / 2}}/{2} + n \cdot m(n-2)$.
nodes.section: 2 The construction of Abbott and Hanson \cite{Abbott}, and Toft \cite{toft2}
nodes.statement_short: Direct count of the AHT hyperedges, summing binomial coefficients up to $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, split by parity of $n$.

nodes.name: ordered set V^1
nodes.statement: Let $V^1 = (v_1, v_2, v_3, \ldots, v_n)$ denote the ordered set where $v_1 \prec v_2 \ldots \prec v_n$.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: swapped indices v_j^p
nodes.statement: For any $1 \leq p \leq n$, let $v_1^p=v_p$, $v_p^1 = v_1$ and $v_j^j = v_j$ for all $j \neq 1,p$.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: ordered set V^p
nodes.statement: Let $V^p$ be the ordered set formed after swapping $v_1$ and $v_p$ of $V^1$. Then, $V^p = (v_1^p, v_2,\ldots, v_{p-1},v_p^1,v_{p+1} \ldots v_n)$ where $v_1^p \prec v_2^p \ldots \prec v_n^p$.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction
nodes.statement_short: $V^p$ is $V^1$ with $v_1$ and $v_p$ swapped.

nodes.name: matching pair in a set-ordered set pair
nodes.statement: For each $1 \leq i \leq n$, we call $u_i \in U$ and $v_i^p \in V^p$ to be a {\it matching pair} of vertices in the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^p$).
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: U_K and V_K^p
nodes.statement: For any $K = \{a_1, a_2, \ldots a_k\}$ which is a proper subset of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ such that $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 \ldots < a_k \leq n$, we denote $U_K = \{u_{a_1}, u_{a_2}, \ldots, u_{a_k}\}$ and $V_K^p = \{v_{a_1}^p, v_{a_2}^p, \ldots, v_{a_k}^p\}$ where $v_{a_1}^p$ is the matching vertex of $u_{a_1}$.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: complements w.r.t. V^p
nodes.statement: We also define ${\bar{U}}_K = U \setminus U_K$ and ${\bar{V}^p_K} = V \setminus V_K^p$.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: First improved construction
nodes.statement: Now we define the construction of the non-$2$-colorable $n$-uniform hypergraph $H$. The vertex set of this hypergraph is $X \cup U \cup V$, and the set of hyperedges is the following:\\ $(i)$ $\{u_i\} \cup e_j \cup \{v_i\}$ for every pair of $i, j$ satisfying $2 \leq i \leq n$ and $1 \leq j \leq m_{n-2}$. $(ii)$ $U$ $(iii)$ $U_K \cup {\bar{V}^p_K}$ for every $1 \leq p \leq n$ and every $K$ such that $|K|$ is odd, and $1 \leq |K| \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. $(iv)$ $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K$ for every $1 \leq p \leq n$ and every $K$ such that $|K|$ is even, and $2 \leq |K| \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction
input: an $(n-2)$-uniform hypergraph producing the best known upper bound for $m(n-2)$
nodes.statement_short: AHT construction with step (i) dropping the pair $(u_1,v_1)$, and steps (iii)-(iv) repeated for every swapped ordering $V^p$.

nodes.name: Count for the first improved construction
nodes.statement: Note that the number of hyperedges formed in step $(i)$ is $(n-1) \cdot m_{n-2}$. Recall that the step $(i)$ of the construction discussed in Section $2$ produces $n \cdot m_{n-2}$ hyperedges and we decrease this number to $(n-1) \cdot m_{n-2}$. The step $(ii)$ of this construction produces a single hyperedge, while steps $(iii)$ and $(iv)$ produce a total of $\binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2} + \ldots + \binom{n}{\lfloor{n/2}\rfloor}$ hyperedges for every $p$ satisfying $1 \leq p \leq n$. Therefore, we obtain:
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction
nodes.statement_short: Count hyperedges per step: $(n-1)m_{n-2}$ in step (i), and $n$ copies of the AHT sets in steps (ii)-(iv).

nodes.name: Preliminary recurrence of the first construction
nodes.statement: $m(n) \leq n \cdot 2^{n-1} - (n-1) + (n-1) \cdot m(n-2)$, when $n$ is odd and,\\ $m(n) \leq n \cdot (2^{n-1} + {n \choose {n / 2}}/{2}) - (n-1) + (n-1) \cdot m(n-2)$, when $n$ is even.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction
nodes.statement_short: Before removing repeated hyperedges, the first construction gives $m(n) \le n2^{n-1}-(n-1)+(n-1)m(n-2)$ for odd $n$.

nodes.name: Observation 1: repeated hyperedges
nodes.statement: Consider the hyperedges formed in the steps $(iii)$ and $(iv)$ of the construction. For any given $p$ satisfying $2 \leq p \leq n$, all the hyperedges which contain both the vertices $u_1$ and $u_p$, or both the vertices $v_1$ and $v_p$ are already formed in the steps $(iii)$ and $(iv)$ for $p = 1$.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction
assumptions: For any given $p$ satisfying $2 \leq p \leq n$
conclusions: all the hyperedges which contain both the vertices $u_1$ and $u_p$, or both the vertices $v_1$ and $v_p$ are already formed in the steps $(iii)$ and $(iv)$ for $p = 1$
nodes.statement_short: For $p\ge 2$, hyperedges of steps (iii)-(iv) containing both $u_1,u_p$ or both $v_1,v_p$ already occur for $p=1$.

nodes.name: Refined count proving Result 1
nodes.statement: The number of hyperedges formed due to the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^1$) is $1 + \binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2} + \ldots + \binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} + (n-1) \cdot m_{n-2}$. The number of new hyperedges formed due to set-ordered set pair ($U,V^p$) for each $2 \leq p \leq n$, is at most $2\cdot\left(1 + \binom{n-2}{1} + \binom{n-2}{2} + \ldots + \binom{n-2}{\lfloor (n-2)/2 \rfloor} \right)$. This is due to the fact that the number of new hyperedges that contains one of the vertices $u_1$ and $u_p$ and are formed in the step $(iii)$ of the construction is $2\cdot\left(1 + \binom{n-2}{2} + \binom{n-2}{4} + \ldots + \binom{n-2}{\lfloor (n-2)/2 \rfloor} \right)$, similarly the number of new hyperedges that contains one of the vertices $v_1$ and $v_p$ and are formed in the step $(iv)$ of the construction is $2\cdot\left(\binom{n-2}{1} + \binom{n-2}{3} + \ldots + \binom{n-2}{\lfloor (n-2)/2 \rfloor} \right)$. Therefore, we obtain:
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction
nodes.statement_short: Count the $p=1$ hyperedges, then bound the new hyperedges for each $p\ge2$ using Observation 1.

nodes.name: Lemma 2: matching-pair coloring lemma
nodes.statement: Consider a coloring $\chi$ of the hypergraph $H$ having the property that there does not exist two different \textit{matching pairs} of vertices ($u_i,v_i^p$) and ($u_j,v_j^p$) in any of the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^p$) such that $u_i$ and $v_i^p$ are colored with Red, and, $u_j$ and $v_j^p$ are colored with Blue in $\chi$. Then, $\chi$ is not a proper $2$-coloring of $H$.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction
assumptions: Consider a coloring $\chi$ of the hypergraph $H$ having the property that there does not exist two different \textit{matching pairs} of vertices ($u_i,v_i^p$) and ($u_j,v_j^p$) in any of the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^p$) such that $u_i$ and $v_i^p$ are colored with Red, and, $u_j$ and $v_j^p$ are colored with Blue in $\chi$.
nodes.statement_short: If no ordering $V^p$ has one all-Red and one all-Blue matching pair, the coloring is not proper.
nodes.label: firstlemma

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Assume for the sake of contradiction that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that there is no \textit{matching pair} ($u_i,v_i^p$) in the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^p$) such that both $u_i$ and $v_i^p$ are colored by Red. Let $U_K$ denote the set of vertices in $U$ which are Red in this coloring, where $K \subseteq \{1, 2, \ldots n\}$ denotes the set of indices of the vertices in the set $U_K$. Note that $U_K$ must be a proper subset of $U$, as $U$ is one of the hyperedges of $H$. Let us consider the following $2$ cases: \begin{itemize} \item \textbf{Case 1: $1 \leq |U_K| < \lfloor n/2\rfloor$} If $|U_K|$ is even, then consider the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K$. All the vertices in this hyperedge are Blue, leading to a contradiction. If $|U_K|$ is odd, then consider the hyperedge $U_K \cup {\bar{V}}_K^p$. At least one of the vertices, say $v_l^p \in {\bar{V}}_K^p$, must have been colored Blue in $\chi$. Consider the vertex $u_l$ such that ($u_l,v_l^p$) is a \textit{matching pair} of vertices in ($U$,$V^p$). It can be seen that the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K \cup \{v_l^p\} \setminus \{u_l\}$ is Blue, leading to a contradiction. \item \textbf{Case 2: $\lfloor n/2\rfloor \leq |U_K| < n$} If $n - |U_K|$ is odd, then consider the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K$. All the vertices in this hyperedge are Blue, leading to a contradiction. If $n - |U_K|$ is even, then consider the hyperedge $U_K \cup {\bar{V}}_K^p$. At least one of the vertices, say $v_l^p \in {\bar{V}}_K^p$, must have been colored by Blue in $\chi$. Consider the vertex $u_l$ such that ($u_l,v_l^p$) is a \textit{matching pair} of vertices in ($U$,$V^p$). It can be seen that the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K \cup \{v_l^p\} \setminus \{u_l\}$ is Blue, leading to a contradiction. $\Box$ \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction with WLOG no Red matching pair; case analysis on $|U_K|$ and its parity exhibits a Blue hyperedge.

nodes.name: Lemma 3: first construction is non-2-colorable
nodes.statement: Our construction produces a hypergraph $H$ with a monochromatic hyperedge under any given Red-Blue coloring of its vertices.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction
conclusions: a hypergraph $H$ with a monochromatic hyperedge under any given Red-Blue coloring of its vertices

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Consider a Red-Blue coloring $\chi$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that the \textit{core hypergraph} $C$ is monochromatic in Red under this coloring $\chi$. Note that the pair ($u_1,v_1$) is not combined with any hyperedge in the \textit{core hypergraph} to form a hyperedge. It can also be noted that any other pair ($u_i,v_i$), $i\not=1$, is combined with every hyperedge in the \textit{core hypergraph}, and therefore both $u_i$ and $v_i$ cannot be colored by Red. \begin{itemize} \item \textbf{Case 1:} If either of $u_1$ or $v_1$ is colored with Blue, then there is no pair ($u_i,v_i$) such that $u_i$ and $v_i$ are both colored by Red. This satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} for the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^1$). Hence, it follows from Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that the hypergraph $H$ is monochromatic under $\chi$. \item \textbf{Case 2:} If both $u_1$ and $v_1$ are colored with Red and if there does not exist any other pair of vertices ($u_i,v_i$) such that both $u_i$ and $v_i$ are colored with Blue, then it satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} for the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^1$). nodes.statement: Assume for the sake of contradiction that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that the non-$2$-colorable core hypergraph $C$ is monochromatic in Red under this coloring $\chi$. Then, none of the matching pair of vertices $u_i$ and $v_i$, $1 \leq i \leq n$, can have both their colors as Blue in $\chi$ as it causes a contradiction to our assumption. Then, it follows from the $p=1$ case of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that all the hyperedges formed in Steps $(v), (vi)$ and $(vii)$ cannot be non-monochromatic under the above condition imposed on $\chi$. This contradicts the assumption that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. $\Box$\\

Similarly, it can be seen from Step $(ii)$ of the construction that the non-$2$-colorable $3$-uniform hypergraph $C$ contains a hyperedge $e^C_{l'} \in E_3$ which is monochromatic in Blue. This contradicts the assumption that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. $\Box$ \\

nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 1: $1 \leq |U_K| < \lfloor n/2\rfloor$} If $|U_K|$ is even, then consider the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K$. All the vertices in this hyperedge are Blue, leading to a contradiction. If $|U_K|$ is odd, then consider the hyperedge $U_K \cup {\bar{V}}_K^p$. At least one of the vertices, say $v_l^p \in {\bar{V}}_K^p$, must have been colored Blue in $\chi$. Consider the vertex $u_l$ such that ($u_l,v_l^p$) is a \textit{matching pair} of vertices in ($U$,$V^p$). It can be seen that the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K \cup \{v_l^p\} \setminus \{u_l\}$ is Blue, leading to a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: When $|U_K|<\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, exhibit a Blue hyperedge.

nodes.name: Case 2: large U_K
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 2: $\lfloor n/2\rfloor \leq |U_K| < n$} If $n - |U_K|$ is odd, then consider the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K$. All the vertices in this hyperedge are Blue, leading to a contradiction. If $n - |U_K|$ is even, then consider the hyperedge $U_K \cup {\bar{V}}_K^p$. At least one of the vertices, say $v_l^p \in {\bar{V}}_K^p$, must have been colored by Blue in $\chi$. Consider the vertex $u_l$ such that ($u_l,v_l^p$) is a \textit{matching pair} of vertices in ($U$,$V^p$). It can be seen that the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K \cup \{v_l^p\} \setminus \{u_l\}$ is Blue, leading to a contradiction. $\Box$
nodes.statement_short: When $|U_K|\ge\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, exhibit a Blue hyperedge.

Consider the vertex $u_l$ such that ($u_l,v_l^p$) is a \textit{matching pair} of vertices in ($U$,$V^p$). It can be seen that the hyperedge $V_K^p \cup {\bar{U}}_K \cup \{v_l^p\} \setminus \{u_l\}$ is Blue, leading to a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Swap a Blue $v_l^p$ for $u_l$ to get a Blue hyperedge.

nodes.name: Setup: core Red
nodes.statement: Consider a Red-Blue coloring $\chi$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that the \textit{core hypergraph} $C$ is monochromatic in Red under this coloring $\chi$. Note that the pair ($u_1,v_1$) is not combined with any hyperedge in the \textit{core hypergraph} to form a hyperedge. It can also be noted that any other pair ($u_i,v_i$), $i\not=1$, is combined with every hyperedge in the \textit{core hypergraph}, and therefore both $u_i$ and $v_i$ cannot be colored by Red.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG the core is Red, so no pair $(u_i,v_i)$, $i\ne1$, is all Red.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: Case 1: u_1 or v_1 Blue
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 1:} If either of $u_1$ or $v_1$ is colored with Blue, then there is no pair ($u_i,v_i$) such that $u_i$ and $v_i$ are both colored by Red. This satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} for the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^1$). Hence, it follows from Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that the hypergraph $H$ is monochromatic under $\chi$.
nodes.statement_short: No Red pair, so Lemma 2 for $V^1$ applies.

nodes.name: Case 2: u_1,v_1 Red, no Blue pair
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 2:} If both $u_1$ and $v_1$ are colored with Red and if there does not exist any other pair of vertices ($u_i,v_i$) such that both $u_i$ and $v_i$ are colored with Blue, then it satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} for the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^1$). Hence, it follows from Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that the hypergraph $H$ is monochromatic under $\chi$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2 for $V^1$ applies.
nodes.section: 3 The first improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: Case 3: u_1,v_1 Red, some Blue pair
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 3:} Let us assume that both $u_1$ and $v_1$ are colored with Red, and there exists at least one other pair ($u_i,v_i$), $i\not=1$, such that both $u_i$ and $v_i$ are colored with Blue. Consider the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^i$). It can be noted that there does not exist any \textit{matching pair} of vertices ($u_j,v_j^i$) in ($U,V^i$) such that both $u_j$ and $v_j^i$ are colored with Red. Hence, it follows from Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that the hypergraph $H$ is monochromatic under $\chi$.
nodes.statement_short: Switch to $V^i$, which has no Red matching pair, and apply Lemma 2.

nodes.name: Relate to AHT
nodes.statement: Note that the Steps $(v)$, $(vi)$ and $(vii)$ in this construction are the same as the Steps $(ii)$, $(iii)$ and $(iv)$ of the construction of Abbott and Hanson \cite{Abbott} which is defined in Section $2$.
nodes.statement_short: Steps (v)-(vii) coincide with the AHT steps.

nodes.name: Count step (i)
nodes.statement: The number of hyperedges formed in Step $(i)$ is $(n-2) \cdot m_{n-2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Step (i) gives $(n-2)m_{n-2}$.

nodes.name: Count steps (ii)-(iv)
nodes.statement: A total of $n \cdot \left( 1 + \binom{n-2}{1} + \binom{n-2}{2} + \ldots + \binom{n-2}{\lfloor (n-2)/2 \rfloor} \right)$ hyperedges are formed in Steps $(ii)$, $(iii)$ and $(iv)$.
nodes.statement_short: $n$ times the $(n-2)$-AHT binomial sum.
nodes.section: 4 Further improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: Count steps (v)-(vii)
nodes.statement: The number of hyperedges formed in Steps $(v)$, $(vi)$ and $(vii)$ is $1 + \binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2} + \ldots + \binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$. Therefore, we obtain:
nodes.statement_short: Add the AHT binomial sum for $n$ and conclude.

nodes.name: Contradiction setup
nodes.statement: Assume for the sake of contradiction that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that the non-$2$-colorable core hypergraph $C$ is monochromatic in Red under this coloring $\chi$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume a proper coloring with the core Red.

nodes.name: No Red primed pair
nodes.statement: Note that none of the matching pair of vertices $u'_i$ and $v'_i$, $1 \leq i \leq (n-2)$, can have both their colors as Red as it causes a contradiction to our assumption due to Step $(i )$ of the construction.
nodes.statement_short: Step (i) forbids an all-Red pair $u'_i,v'_i$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2 to primed layer
nodes.statement: Therefore, it follows from the $p=1$ case of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that at least one of the $(n-2)$-uniform sets formed in the Steps $(ii), (iii)$ and $(iv)$ (after excluding the vertices $u_i$ and $v_i$, $1 \leq i \leq n$) of the construction must be monochromatic under the given coloring $\chi$.
nodes.statement_short: Some $(n-2)$-set from steps (ii)-(iv) is monochromatic.
nodes.section: 4 Further improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: No Blue pair
nodes.statement: Without the loss of generality, let us assume that it is monochromatic in Blue. Then, none of the matching pair of vertices $u_i$ and $v_i$, $1 \leq i \leq n$, can have both their colors as Blue in $\chi$ as it causes a contradiction to our assumption.
nodes.statement_short: With that set Blue, no pair $u_i,v_i$ is all Blue.
nodes.section: 4 Further improvement over the AHT construction

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2 to U,V
nodes.statement: Then, it follows from the $p=1$ case of Lemma \ref{firstlemma} that all the hyperedges formed in Steps $(v), (vi)$ and $(vii)$ cannot be non-monochromatic under the above condition imposed on $\chi$.
nodes.statement_short: Steps (v)-(vii) then contain a monochromatic hyperedge.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: This contradicts the assumption that $\chi$ is a proper $2$-coloring of $H$. $\Box$
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction.

nodes.name: Count steps (i)-(ii)
nodes.statement: The number of hyperedges formed in Step $(i)$ is $m(5) \cdot m(3) \leq 357$. The same number of hyperedges is formed in Step $(ii)$.
nodes.statement_short: Each of steps (i), (ii) gives $m(5)m(3)\le357$.

nodes.name: Count steps (iii)-(vi)
nodes.statement: The Step $(iii)$ produces $8 \cdot m(3) \cdot m(3) \leq 392$ hyperedges, while a single hyperedge is formed in Step $(iv)$. The Steps $(v)$ and $(vi)$ produce a total of $\binom{8}{1} + \binom{8}{2} + \binom{8}{3} + \binom{8}{4}$ hyperedges.
